name: Dense data
summary: Compact, exact and quiet, for analysts who scan alerts and compare signals all day.
description: Dense data is an Open DS scheme: a full set of answers to the Open DS grammar, with the reasons behind each, usage rules, voice and tone, and the tokens that follow. Compact, exact and quiet, for analysts who scan alerts and compare signals all day.

ai.use_when: Security operations, threat detection, model monitoring, admin panels and analytics: many records, daily expert users, mouse and keyboard.
ai.avoid_when: Public sites, reading products, or first-time visitors on phones.

scenarios.text: A security analyst opens the alert queue at 8:00 and scans 200 rows for escalated threats.
An analyst compares this week's detections with last week's, model by model and column by column.

summary.text: Terse and exact. Say what happened and what to do, in as few words as possible.

out.why: Slides hide items, and most people never reach the later ones. Dense data's experts want many records on one screen.
A drawer is for phones. Dense data's experts work at a desk with a mouse and keyboard, and the scheme avoids first-time visitors on phones.
Native select is best on phones, and Dense data runs at a desk. Its select already picks one value. A small team keeps fewer parts right.
Navigation menu is for the sections of a website. Dense data avoids public sites, and its app navigation stays open all shift in a sidebar.

answers.question: brand.q3
answers.why: IBM Plex Sans for every text role and IBM Plex Mono for data: exact and quiet, so the numbers stay the hero.

considers.readability: Plex Sans is a neutral grotesque with open shapes, made for screens; it reads at the small body size dense rows need.
considers.legibility: Data, codes and IDs sit in Plex Mono, where each character holds its own fixed cell, so they read character by character.
considers.scalability: Plex ships a full range of weights, so every role in the type scale has its own weight without a second sans.
considers.numerals: Digits in Plex Mono are all one width, so columns of numbers line up.
considers.scripts: Plex Sans covers Latin, Cyrillic and Greek; Hebrew, Arabic and other scripts come as sister families of IBM Plex, drawn to match.
considers.recognition: One family with a matching mono gives the product an engineered, consistent voice.
considers.familiarity: A grotesque reads as standard and trusted in operations tools.
considers.personality: Precise, as the brand answer asks, and quiet, so the brand steps back.
considers.performance: Two families; load only the weights the scale uses.
considers.licensing: SIL Open Font License: free to embed in apps and on the web.
considers.fallback: Falls back to system-ui and ui-monospace, as its tokens say; Plex Mono is its own pair.

color.$description: Color options: raw hue ramps. Each hue has a light ramp and a dark ramp (the same steps tuned for dark backgrounds). Steps only: each theme decides its own base (@). Themes pick from these; components never read them.

slate.$description: The slate hue: a light ramp, a dark ramp and its base value.

150.$description: Derived: the step between 100 and 200 on the scheme's step curve (strong-ease), even in contrast. Added so a floating layer sits one step above raised in dark.

400.$description: Derived: the OKLab midpoint of 300 and 500. Added so muted text can pass 4.5:1 and stay quieter than secondary.

600.$description: Derived: the OKLab midpoint of 500 and 700. Added so muted text can pass 4.5:1 and stay quieter than secondary.

150.$description: Derived: the step between 100 and 200 on the scheme's step curve (strong-ease), even in contrast. Added so a floating layer sits one step above raised in dark. Moved 0.015 darker in OKLab lightness, so muted text keeps its 4.5:1 floor on a floating layer, with a 0.1 margin.

400.$description: Derived: the OKLab midpoint of 300 and 500. Added so muted text can pass 4.5:1 and stay quieter than secondary.

600.$description: Derived: the OKLab midpoint of 500 and 700. Added so muted text can pass 4.5:1 and stay quieter than secondary.

floor.$description: Derived: step 0 at 0.04 lower OKLab lightness, its hue and chroma kept. Added so a dark well sits below a canvas on 0.

violet.$description: The violet hue: a light ramp, a dark ramp and its base value.

green.$description: The green hue: a light ramp, a dark ramp and its base value.

100.why: This step is the soft background of status messages in light mode and the status text in dark mode. As generated, the text looked white on dark backgrounds, so the step got a little more color, and blue and red a touch darker, until the color showed.

space.$description: Space options. Names give the size in pixels at the default text size; values are rem.

size.$description: Size options for controls, rows and icons.

round.$description: A circle of a square: avatars, radio dots, thumbs and round buttons.

pill.$description: A capsule of any box: tracks, progress, the scroll thumb and pill controls.

size.$description: Type size options. Names are pixels at the default text size; values are rem, so text grows with the user's setting.

line-height.$description: Line height options: ratios of the text size. The type scale generates them.

line-box.$description: Line box options: one line's height, in rem. The type scale generates them.

family.$description: Font family options. Each brand's theme picks its display, body, interface and data fonts from these.

open-ds.why: IBM Plex Sans's x-height is 0.516 of the em (its metrics: 516 of 1000 units), so 12px text has a 6.2px x-height.

fast.$description: Fast: about 120ms, the convention for feedback.

standard.$description: A standard ease-out: fast at the start, settling slowly, with no overshoot.

strong-out.$description: A strong ease-out: most of the way in the first third of the time, then a soft stop. For exits.

shadow.$description: Raw shadows. Elevation semantics point at these.

overlay.$description: Raw shadow for overlay in light mode.

overlay-dark.$description: Raw shadow for overlay in dark mode.

1_5.$description: An icon stroke width option, on Lucide's 24px grid.

open-ds.why: A pointer target sets the 32px default. Compact is one 8px step below it; large equals the default, as the scheme has no hero action. Rows are a decision of their own and stay one control tall.
Compact: more records fit on one screen, so components keep their tightest spacing.
